newsitem.title: USA: AMEX plans fund linked to Dow Jones average-Syron.
newsitem.headline: AMEX plans fund linked to Dow Jones average-Syron.

text.p: The American Stock Exchange (Amex) is developing a new exchange trade fund based on the Dow Jones Industrial Average which will enable investors to buy shares of the famous stock index, Amex chairman Richard Syron said.

Amex is waiting for U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) approval of the fund, which it expects to launch in the fourth quarter for institutional and individual investors. Syron said he expected the new trade fund to expand liquidity and encourage trading on the American Stock Exchange.
"The new product will be coming out towards the end of this year and that will give an investor a way to take a position ... efficiently in the entire Dow," Syron told Reuters.

The product, which still does not have a name, will work like an ordinary index mutual fund, except it will trade and price throughout the trading session like a single-share stock that follows the Dow Jones Industrial Average swings during the day.
The new product will work in a similar fashion to the so-called Spider, which is an exchange trade fund based on the Standard and Poor's 500 Index.
Syron also said he expected to have about 90 new listings this year at the Amercian Stock Exchange.
"This is our best performance, I think, in 10 years ... For an organization which has basically around 700 companies, that's not a bad percentage increase," Syron said.
